rules.interaction: Statewide antitrust rule; does not displace local rules and states it does not limit other antitrust laws.
rules.title: AB 325: unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a price-fixing agreement or conspiracy, or to coerce another person to adopt the prices it recommends. A common pricing algorithm is any software or method used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend or influence a price.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data (agreement or coercion)
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm; not limited to housing, so covers rent-setting software
rules.exemptions: End consumers are not a covered person
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

notes: Chaptered 2025-10-06 (Ch. 338); the text gives no effective date, so effective_date is null (status in_force assumes the usual January 2026 start, UNVERIFIED from this doc). Sec. 16756.1 (pleading standard) is procedural and merged here.
